tree: every file: node "rig" (turns the game's axes to y up, facing +z, metres), then the game's bones by name; do not animate "rig". The same tree as assets/range.

clip_fields.loop: first and last pose within 2 degrees and 5 mm: play it round
clip_fields.pingpong: it does not close: play it forward then backward
clip_fields.holds_weapon: the clip was authored with a weapon in the hands (see weapon, hands_note)
clip_fields.facing_deg: which way the chest faces on average, about the up axis: 0 is +z, positive is a turn to the figure's own left (+x). Turn the figure by minus this to square it up
clip_fields.roams_m: how far the pelvis wanders over the floor during the clip
clip_fields.feet_leave_floor_m: how high the lower foot gets: a jump
clip_fields.hands: each hand's average place from the feet (forward +z, left +x, up +y, metres), its lowest and highest, and how far the fingers curl from flat, least and most, in degrees

notes: The DJ is the agent whose English name is "Sir Bloody Miami Darryl | The Professionals": resource/csgo_english.txt: CSGO_Customplayer_tm_professional_varf; scripts/items/items_game.txt: item 4726 "customplayer_tm_professional_varf", model_player.

All nine clips are the game's own, undoctored, on the same skeleton as the range's clips (animation/skeletons/characters/worldmodel.vnmskel; all 775 clips under ui_anims/, world/shared/, world/equipment/ and world/grenade/ name it).

stand_* and cheer_* are end-of-match celebration clips (ui_anims/end_round/celebrate): no weapon skeleton is attached to them and the hands open and close freely, so they are read as empty-handed. Each starts and ends in its character's rest pose, so they loop, but a cheer is a rest, a gesture, and a rest again, not a continuous dance.
The names stand_/cheer_ and the descriptions in "does" are my reading of the stick figures and the Blender renders, not the game's names.

dj_1 and dj_2 are STAND-INS: the game has no animation of a person working a desk. They are the main-menu idle of a Terrorist holding an M249 at the hip, and a variation of it in which he looks down at the gun and lifts it. The fingers are curled round a gun that is not there and the hands will not land on anything exactly.

A desk for the DJ, from dj_1: the wrists are 1.11 m (right) and 1.13 m (left) above the floor, 0.24 and 0.20 m in front of the feet, and 0.59 m apart; in dj_2 they lift to 1.48 m. A top a little under the wrists is my suggestion, not a number from the game.
Clips made for different characters start from different rest poses: anims.same_rest_pose groups the ones that share one; cross-fade between groups.
The agent's height_m is measured as the range's are, in the rifle idle (a slight stoop); upright_top_m is the top of the hair standing in stand_1, measured in Blender.
Twist, shoulder-blade and jiggle bones have no tracks and stay at rest, as on the range's agents. Head ball, roughness and skin are as make_agents does them.
Blood decals are exported as the game stores them: the colour texture is already a dark red in the red channel alone with the shape in alpha. Only resized (1024 to 512).

Blood spray, trail and mist sprites are grey in the game with the shape in alpha and are coloured when drawn. Converted: RGB is that grey times one blood red (tint_rgb, taken from the particle definition), alpha kept. The game runs the grey through a colour gradient instead; which end of the gradient is which is not something I could read, so one colour stands for it.

Exported sprites are the medium impact's: blood_spray_top (spray), blood_spray_med (trail: the game draws these stretched along the particle's path) and the steam flipbook its mist uses (2 of its 4 sequences). The low and high impacts use blood_spray_low / _high for their trails, not exported.
Flipbook frames are stored cropped and packed; each was put back into its full cell (from the sheet's cropped and uncropped rectangles) and laid out in an even grid, left to right, top to bottom.

Which of blood_impact_low / med / high a bullet plays, and what the control points mean (the sprays fly along +x of control point 2, the "away" mist along -x), is decided in code: read as "toward the shooter" and "out the back", a guess.
A wall decal's size in the world is not in its material or in decalgroups.vdata. The floor decal a spray leaves is a particle of radius 30 to 40 units (blood_impact_med_ground_decal.vpcf).

Particle attribute numbers were read as: 1 lifetime, 3 radius, 4 roll, 7 alpha, 9 sequence, 10 trail length, 12 yaw, 38 the place in the flipbook (the values fit; 38 runs 0 to 1 over the life and the renderers use manual frames); others are left numbered in blood/particles.json.
count per_detail_level is [LOD0..LOD3] as the file has it; taken as more particles at a higher particle detail setting.
